One Information Marketplace end-to-end slice delivery: a buyer publishes an ECDH recipient public key (private half stays on the buyer device); on owner approval the seller device seals the requested safe-summary slice against that key and posts a ciphertext envelope, which the buyer fetches and decrypts locally from the Received-data surface.

One Information Marketplace proactive opportunity nudges: the server derives dateless intent signals from the owner's publishable-slice metadata (and the client may post dated expiry signals), surfaced as flashcards on Agent One where the owner publishes, snoozes, or dismisses them; state is read and mutated server-side per owner.

One Information Marketplace access-request inbox: a buyer files a request for owner-approved access to a published data-slice safe projection; the owner lists, approves, or denies server-side from the marketplace surface or via Agent One over A2A.

Kai analyze ("debate") resumable-run store added in migration 125. The analyze run manager writes exactly one terminal-checkpoint row per run at the completed/failed/canceled transition and reads it back only when a resumed GET /run/{id}/stream lands on a Cloud Run instance that never created the run, replaying the already-delivered terminal DecisionCard instead of returning ANALYZE_RUN_NOT_FOUND. Gated by KAI_ANALYZE_DURABLE_RUN_STORE (default off); when off no row is ever written or read.
Plaid link, refresh, portfolio source preference, and portfolio-read services
user-consented Gmail receipt sync and receipt-memory preview services
Historical recipient-key metadata retained solely for completed CRM-ZK and CRM-ZK-UAT workflow history; no active runtime, route, or registry loader reads these tables.
bounded legacy-to-PKM compatibility and account deletion cleanup only
market/reference lookup, cache refresh, and Kai market insight services
One action directive issuance, confirmation, exactly-once consumption, settlement, cancellation, and expiry
message feedback service, written from the Agent One chat thumbs control via /api/one/agent-chat/feedback and read for response-quality reporting
model preference service, read on every agent chat turn and written from Agent chat or /api/one/models/preference

One mailbox intake, account-scoped automatic-preparation preference, KYC workflow status, per-user public client connector metadata, consent continuation, transient approved Gmail send, and encrypted PKM writeback receipt

One Location Agent verified-recipient directory, server-owned and revocable automatic-approval preferences, owner-selected Save My Soul contacts, named-Circle join-code workflows, recipient public key registration, owner-approved grants, encrypted envelope writes, authenticated recipient ciphertext reads, UAT-only short-lived nearby check-in with alias-based Connect requests, public request invites, Invite to One network onboarding, referrals, revocation, expiry, and metadata-only audit

Authenticated One Location People-tab Circle creation, code join, targeted existing-direct-connection invitation and acceptance, membership listing, removal, leave, and deletion workflows. Code join or targeted-invite acceptance creates source-aware canonical mutual connection origins with every active Circle member; creating a targeted invitation alone creates no membership or connection.

Short-lived ledger of completed nearby check-in visits, so the place a person just left can be rated and so the check-in travel-continuity guard survives a checkout that clears the presence anchor. The venue is readable only as an AES-256-GCM envelope bound by AAD to its owner, alongside a server-keyed equality token that allows same-venue and distinct-place checks without decryption.

One 1-5 star rating per person per place, private to its author and readable only by them, plus an anonymous per-place count and sum derived from those rows. This is the only durable person-to-venue link in One Location and is created solely on acceptance of the named, versioned consent one-location-place-rating-v1. It stores no review text, no author display identity, and no author reference reaches any cross-user projection; the aggregate holds no user reference at all and is withheld below five raters and reported in buckets.
Authenticated person-profile and Agent One workflows that prepare, create, inspect, cancel, expire, revoke, and export viewer-to-owner consent requests using opaque consumer scope references.

One referral program: server-minted public attribution slugs, pre-authentication attribution records bound to a canonical user only after sign-in, one referrer-to-referred relationship per referred user, server-calculated agent engagement sessions, an append-only idempotent event ledger, versioned qualification policy, and the human risk-review queue. Read by the Profile Referrals tab as aggregate counts and status words only.

Vault-owner Wallet Profile controls create, edit, pause, resume, rotate, and revoke one card per account; the Apple Wallet pass and the public /c/{token} page resolve that card unauthenticated by SHA-256 hash of the presented share token, through the same projection builder the owner's preview-as-visitor uses
Feature-flagged personal-agent reservation, BYOC setup, provider provisioning, lifecycle replay, and the parked provider-deprovision intent design
per-user sovereign-agent provisioning/deprovision and status services (flag-off, PERSONAL_AGENT_ENABLED)
vault-owner profile controls publish safe public-profile projections; authenticated developer connectors read them by opaque handle through the public-profile export endpoint
PKM coherent snapshot, atomic store, owner rollback, delete-domain routes, and client-side vault unlock flows
PKM metadata, scope discovery, manifest repair, and replay/audit services
client-side PKM cutover, server-issued upgrade claims, idempotent commit receipts, and generic PKM upgrade orchestration
the owner's own Personal World Model doc behind /api/pwm (cross-device preference sync)
RIA marketplace qualified investor deck, public discovery cards, and official SEC filing evidence

Cross-instance one-time nonce registry for signed One voice relay tickets (migration 084). consume_relay_ticket_shared() in api/routes/one/relay_auth.py enforces single use globally via INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; a conflicting insert means replay. Expired rows are pruned opportunistically by expiry scan. Scale-plane doctrine: Postgres now, Redis SETNX-with-TTL later behind the same seam.
RIA profile, marketplace deck actions, client relationship, bilateral connection-scope proposal, invite, and share-grant services
PCHP RFC-002 subscription grants: owner-issued, subscriber-scoped read access to PWM fields (/api/fabric/grants)
PCHP RFC-002 hash-chained receipt ledger for grant/read/revoke events (/api/fabric/receipts)
brand-initiated PCHP RFC-002 pairing requests: create, code lookup, approve/deny, single handle claim (/api/fabric/requests)

Generalized directional trusted-connection graph. Written only via Agent One (add/remove/list intents delegated to the agent_connections lane) and via circle-invite claim (one-way claimer→inviter edge); read in-process by any backend agent (e.g. Location, Email) through TrustedConnectionsService for SOS recipient resolution and check-in targeting. People are resolved read-only through the One Location verified-recipient directory. Supersedes the former one_location_network_connections table; its forward-only removal is pending live row-count, retention, and backup preflight.
Metadata-only trusted-device authorization, challenge, capability issuance, use, and revocation audit events written by TrustedDeviceService.
Short-lived PKCE authorization codes and single-use proof-of-possession challenges consumed atomically through TrustedDeviceService.

First-party Hermes device registration, listing, proof-of-possession lookup, last-used and last-synced tracking, revocation, advisory remote-revoke seal telemetry, and advisory liveness heartbeats through TrustedDeviceService.

Two-way mutual connection graph. connection_requests holds the directional handshake; connections is the canonical pair projection; connection_origins is the durable source ledger for direct requests, legacy invites, imports, viewer-relative contact_sync provenance, and one or more named Circles. Contact sync uses the visible verified-phone Connect-directory default under contact_directory_auto_connect_v2, honors explicit contact opt-out and marketplace hide, revalidates each submitted digest against the current unique verified phone, and writes every eligible non-suppressed match as canonical graph projections transactionally. Policy writers and graph activation share a per-user database lock. Viewer-relative provenance records the directory policy and actual preference state without fabricating historical consent evidence. contact_sync_lookup_budgets is the Postgres-authoritative cross-instance abuse-budget seam; SlowAPI is only the outer request-count guard. Named Circle join/accept writes only named_circle origins. The canonical pair remains active while any origin is active.
vault setup, unlock-status, wrapper selection, and account deletion services
server-side WebAuthn/FIDO2 registration and authentication ceremony (flag-off, WEBAUTHN_ENABLED; migration parked)
